_what: CONTENT DELTA for schema/class-frame-v1.json — appliances, a correction pass across the four earlier systems, and an outside-review pass. NOT purely append-only.
_why: Two authors. Builder Code owns the structure; the design session owns the five content arrays.
_cutFrom: the 79-class state as merged in PR #63, read from the source.
_noStatusBlock: Derived and tested since PR #61. `contentPassProgress.remaining` needs `appliances` dropped by hand.

_threePassesInOneDelta.1_theCorrectionPass: The owner's gas fireplace example: across four systems the design session wrote the care a TRADE performs and under-wrote the care a HOUSEHOLD performs. Ten classes were missing household care.
_threePassesInOneDelta.2_theReasonPass: Answering Builder Code's PR #63 question — can a reader tell a ruling from unwritten — required writing a REASON for every zero-care class. That found five more omissions: a lake intake is pulled before ice, a cistern is cleaned, a condensate reservoir grows biofilm, baseboard fins collect dust, a stovepipe is swept with the chimney. **Found by having to justify the emptiness, not by reviewing it** — rule 9 applied to content.
_threePassesInOneDelta.3_theOutsideReviewPass: One model, one framing, appliances only, no vocabulary shown — anti-anchoring per rule 11b. Six real misses from 21 classes, and they share a shape: **the design session wrote the care visible on the OUTSIDE of an appliance and under-wrote the care that involves REMOVING or EMPTYING something.** Gasket, coil and glass are visible; filter, trap, drain and defrost are not. That is now a third question asked of every class in the remaining systems.

_theMostValuableSingleCorrection: `washer-top-load` declared zero care WITH A STATED REASON, and the reason was wrong — a top-loader runs a tub-clean cycle and many carry a pump trap. **A ruling with a reason is harder to catch than an omission**, because it looks considered. Neither internal pass found it; outside review did, on its first use.
_whatOutsideReviewMostlyProduced: Procedures, not categories, despite the prompt asking for categories — sixteen lines for a refrigerator collapsing to four categories. Worth recording rather than discarding: **that is exactly the model-specific detail layer §4's research pass is designed to generate at runtime**, produced unprompted and sourced to manufacturer documentation. The two-layer design was confirmed from outside by accident.

_twoScopeQuestionsNotDecidedHere.induction: v0.2 merged induction into `range-electric-smoothtop` on the argument that ceramic and induction share glass-top care exactly. Outside review says their ventilation and cooling-air requirements differ. **The same shape as the coil-range lesson running the other direction** — a merge made on a shared-care argument that may miss a difference. Not decided; recorded.
_twoScopeQuestionsNotDecidedHere.heatPumpDryer: Genuinely different care — condenser coil and condensate. Prevalence in the region is the open question, not the care.

careCategories.label: Door seal cleaning
careCategories.note: Household-level, frequent, and it is what makes a gasket last. Shared across refrigeration, dishwashers and front-load washers.

careCategories.label: Grease filter cleaning
careCategories.note: Household-level and monthly in a kitchen that cooks.

careCategories.label: Charcoal filter replacement
careCategories.note: Recirculating hoods. Consumable — §1b part identity. Nobody replaces it, which is why it is declared.

careCategories.label: Lint and duct clearing
careCategories.note: The dryer duct's whole reason for existing as a class.

careCategories.label: Drum and gasket service
careCategories.note: Front-load washers. Leaving the door ajar is half of it and costs nothing.

careCategories.label: Appliance descaling
careCategories.note: Dishwashers and kettles in hard water. Distinct from `descale`, which is a heat exchanger.

careCategories.label: Interior cleaning
careCategories.note: Household-level. Ovens, refrigerators, microwaves — the care that keeps a thing working rather than merely clean.

careCategories.label: Glass and surface care
careCategories.note: Smooth-top ranges and cooktops need a specific cleaner and a scraper; the wrong one scratches. Also gas fireplace glass.

careCategories.label: Drip pan replacement
careCategories.note: Coil ranges and cooktops. Consumable — §1b, and the part number is why the coil-versus-smooth split earns itself.

careCategories.label: Appliance condenser coil cleaning
careCategories.note: Refrigeration. Distinct from `coil-cleaning`, which is an HVAC coil in an airstream.

careCategories.label: Seasonal removal and reinstallation
careCategories.note: Pulled before ice and returned after. Lake intakes and floating docks — a whole category the first four systems missed because it is care that happens to a thing rather than on it.

careCategories.label: Drain filter or trap cleaning
careCategories.note: A debris trap in a drain path — a dishwasher filter, a front-load washer pump trap. Owner-accessible on most models, neglected on nearly all. Added 2026-08-05 from outside review.

careCategories.label: Running the appliance's own cleaning cycle
careCategories.note: Tub-clean, clean-washer, self-clean oven. Distinct from `interior-cleaning`: this is the appliance cleaning itself on a rhythm somebody has to remember, which is why it is the one that gets skipped. Added 2026-08-05.

careCategories.label: Manual defrosting
careCategories.note: Non-frost-free freezers and refrigerators. Chest freezers are common in rural stock. Added 2026-08-05.

careCategories.label: Exterior vent termination clearing
careCategories.note: Snow, ice, nests, leaves, and a backdraft damper that must move freely. Cross-system — dryers, range hoods, and bathroom fans when interior is written. Added 2026-08-05; the frame had the inspection point and not the task.

inspectionPoints.label: Levelling and stability
inspectionPoints.note: An unlevel range is a tipping hazard and an unlevel washer walks itself apart.

inspectionPoints.label: Anti-tip bracket present
inspectionPoints.note: Ranges. Cheap, invisible, and the failure it prevents involves a child and a hot oven.

inspectionPoints.label: Supply line and shutoff condition
inspectionPoints.note: Braided lines age. This is the single commonest source of an unattended flood in a house.

inspectionPoints.label: Duct run and termination
inspectionPoints.note: Dryer ducts. Length, material and where it actually ends — a run into a soffit is common and wrong.

inspectionPoints.label: Ambient temperature suitability
inspectionPoints.note: A refrigerator in an unheated Ontario garage stops cooling in winter unless it carries a kit — §1.2's exposure exception, made checkable.

inspectionPoints.label: Gas connection and shutoff
inspectionPoints.note: Gas ranges and dryers. Visual only; anything beyond looking is a gas fitter's, which the owner has ruled HouseSteady cannot do at all.

opportunityConditions.label: Water-supplied appliance with no leak protection
opportunityConditions.note: A washer, dishwasher or fridge line with no pan, no sensor and no auto-shutoff. Cheap, and the failure it prevents is the expensive one.

opportunityConditions.label: Dryer duct run longer or more restrictive than intended
Recirculating hood filter never replaced
opportunityConditions.note: Fires on almost every recirculating hood, which is the point of declaring it.

ownerQuestions.label: Does it still do what you need it to?
ownerQuestions.note: Households know an appliance is failing long before it fails, and it appears in no record. It is also the least intrusive way to ask about age.

ownerQuestions.label: Has it ever flooded or overflowed?
Do you use it?
ownerQuestions.note: A second fridge nobody opens, a wall oven used twice a year. It changes the care that is worth doing and the replacement horizon that is worth stating.

classes.label: Refrigerator
classes.note: Four care categories, all household-level and all frequent. The water filter is the consumable and carries a part identity. Manual defrost added 2026-08-05 for non-frost-free models.

classes.label: Garage refrigerator
classes.note: §1.2's exposure exception working. An ambient-temperature kit and cold-weather coil behaviour a kitchen unit never needs — and the failure is silent, because it stops cooling in the season nobody opens it. Manual defrost added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Freezer
classes.note: Stub component type at v1.11.0 — reported, not an error. Fifth stub. Manual defrost added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Dishwasher
classes.note: Drain filter added 2026-08-05 — the most-neglected recurring item in a modern kitchen.

classes.label: Gas range
classes.note: Its care is the household's entirely. Anything at the gas connection beyond looking is a gas fitter's — HouseSteady labour cannot do gas work at all, per the owner 2026-08-05. Self-clean cycle added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Coil-top electric range
classes.note: The split three outside reviewers missed. Drip pans are a consumable with a part number and elements unplug — neither exists on a smooth-top, and `glass-and-surface-care` does not apply here at all. Self-clean cycle added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Smooth-top electric range
classes.note: Absorbs induction — ceramic and induction share glass-top care exactly. A specific cleaner and a scraper; the wrong cleaner scratches. Self-clean cycle added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Recirculating range hood
classes.note: Charcoal filter, no duct — and nobody replaces it, which is why the opportunity fires on almost every one.

classes.label: Over-range microwave
classes.note: Often doubles as the hood, which is why it carries hood care rather than microwave care alone.

classes.label: Front-load washer
classes.note: Gasket and drum care a top-loader has no equivalent of, and the whole of the split. Pump trap and tub-clean cycle added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Top-load washer
classes.note: Zero care categories, and it is a ruling: a top-loader has no gasket to dry and no drum cycle to run. Its whole risk is the supply line, which is inspection. CORRECTED 2026-08-05 by outside review, and this is the one that matters: it declared zero care with a stated reason, and the reason was wrong. A top-loader runs a tub-clean cycle and many carry a pump trap. A ruling with a reason is harder to catch than an omission, which is exactly why it was caught from outside rather than by the internal pass.

classes.label: Electric dryer
classes.note: Drum and moisture-sensor cleaning, and termination clearing, added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Gas dryer
classes.note: A gas connection and a different venting risk — the split earns itself on one inspection point and a fuel HouseSteady labour cannot touch. Drum and moisture-sensor cleaning, and termination clearing, added 2026-08-05.

classes.label: Dryer duct
classes.note: The highest-consequence unglamorous item in the house. No replacement horizon — a duct is rerouted or corrected, never replaced on a lifespan. Termination clearing added 2026-08-05 — the frame had the inspection point and not the task.

classes.label: Central vacuum
classes.note: Common in 1990s–2010s stock and ignored until suction dies.

classes.label: Food waste disposer
classes.note: Added 2026-08-05 from outside review. Common, absent from v0.2 entirely, and it sits on the boundary between appliances and plumbing — filed here because it is an appliance, and flagged in case plumbing wants it.

_modifiedClasses.label: Heat pump water heater
_modifiedClasses.note: It cools and dehumidifies the room it stands in — welcome in July, a real load in January. Corrected 2026-08-05 — it has an appliance condenser coil and the household can clean it.

_modifiedClasses.label: Hot water recirculation pump
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling: a sealed circulator runs to failure and is replaced, never serviced.

_modifiedClasses.label: Expansion tank
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care and two inspection points, and one of the higher-value rows in the system — it fails invisibly and the symptom reads as a bad relief valve. Zero care is a ruling.

_modifiedClasses.label: Well pump — submersible
_modifiedClasses.note: Split from `well-pump` at pass two. It is in the well and cannot be looked at — for a service whose product is documentation, observable-versus-not is the sharpest split there is. Zero care is a ruling and it follows from where it lives — a pump in a well cannot be reached to be maintained.

_modifiedClasses.label: Well pump — jet
_modifiedClasses.note: The other half of the split. In the basement and inspectable, which is the whole difference. Zero care is a ruling: reachable but sealed. Service is a trade call on a symptom, not a rhythm.

_modifiedClasses.label: Well pressure switch
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling — contacts pit and the switch is replaced; nothing is maintained.

_modifiedClasses.label: Low-water protection
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling: a protective device that is tested rather than maintained.

_modifiedClasses.label: Well pressure tank
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling. Pre-charge is a measurement; correcting it is a trade task fired by the finding, not a rhythm.

_modifiedClasses.label: Booster pump
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling — sealed, and replaced rather than serviced.

_modifiedClasses.label: Lake water intake
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05 — an intake line is pulled before ice and returned after. Declared zero care until the reason had to be written down, and there was no reason.

_modifiedClasses.label: Cistern
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05 — a cistern is cleaned and disinfected on a rhythm.

_modifiedClasses.label: Water softener
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05 — the brine tank is household work beyond salt and bridging.

_modifiedClasses.label: Iron filter
_modifiedClasses.note: Stub type at config v1.11.0 — reported, not an error. Zero care is a ruling: it backwashes itself, and media replacement is a trade task on a multi-year horizon rather than care.

_modifiedClasses.label: UV sterilizer
_modifiedClasses.note: A spent lamp keeps glowing. The schedule has no recurring item for it at all — this is where the engine earns its place in this system. Corrected 2026-08-05 — housing wipe-down at lamp change.

_modifiedClasses.label: Water treatment system
_modifiedClasses.note: Declares zero care by design — this kind of thing bears no dependable maintenance and saying so is the point. The fifth output rescued it: its most useful question is whether the household can name it. Zero care is a ruling.

_modifiedClasses.label: Distribution box
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling — a d-box is inspected and levelled when found wrong, never maintained.

_modifiedClasses.label: Leaching or filter bed
_modifiedClasses.note: componentType `none`, resolving F-30. A bed is an area, not a point — no lid checklist applies to it, and `none` needs no config change. Its inspection points come from this class, and every one is `direct`. Zero care is a ruling and it is the whole point of the class: a bed is protected, not maintained. Everything that helps it is something not done to it.

_modifiedClasses.label: Septic alarm
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling — tested, not maintained.

_modifiedClasses.label: Septic pump chamber
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling: the chamber is a vessel. Its pump is a separate class.

_modifiedClasses.label: Effluent pump
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling — sealed and submerged, serviced only when pulled.

_modifiedClasses.label: Circulator pump
_modifiedClasses.note: A boiler may have several and any one failing disables a zone — which is why the owner question about a cold room is on the radiator and the boiler both. Zero care is a ruling: modern circulators are sealed and maintenance-free by design.

_modifiedClasses.label: Window air conditioner
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05 — an appliance coil, not an airstream coil.

_modifiedClasses.label: Whole-home dehumidifier
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05.

_modifiedClasses.label: Portable dehumidifier
_modifiedClasses.note: No checklist, and it has a filter nobody cleans. Corrected 2026-08-05 — bucket and coil are household care, and `coil-cleaning` was the wrong token: this is an appliance coil.

_modifiedClasses.label: Register or grille
_modifiedClasses.note: Merged supply and return at v0.2 — they share every care task, and balance is a property-level diagnostic the property pass handles rather than object care. No replacement horizon: a grille is replaced when a room is renovated, not on a lifespan. Zero care is a ruling.

_modifiedClasses.label: Condensate pump
_modifiedClasses.note: Fails silently and floods the mechanical room while the appliance it serves is fine. Corrected 2026-08-05 — the reservoir grows biofilm and clearing it is household work.

_modifiedClasses.label: Electric baseboard heater
_modifiedClasses.note: Very common in older rural stock and in additions. Corrected 2026-08-05 — the fins collect dust and vacuuming them is household work that measurably affects output.

_modifiedClasses.label: Wood-burning fireplace
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05.

_modifiedClasses.label: Wood stove
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05 — door glass is household care, distinct from the sweep.

_modifiedClasses.label: Pellet stove
_modifiedClasses.note: Its care is unlike a wood stove's — a blower, an auger and a burn pot, and no creosote point because it vents differently. Corrected 2026-08-05.

_modifiedClasses.label: Gas fireplace
_modifiedClasses.note: Corrected 2026-08-05. Declared only the annual service until the owner pointed out that glass, logs and dust are real recurring care and the household's. The trade question was asked and the household question was not.

_modifiedClasses.label: Electric fireplace
_modifiedClasses.note: Almost no care and no inspection point that is not a general electrical one. Worth the class precisely to say so — an empty row is an answer. Zero care is a ruling.

_modifiedClasses.label: Chimney cap
_modifiedClasses.note: Separately replaceable, and animals and water get in while the chimney itself is sound. Zero care is a ruling — a cap is inspected and replaced, never serviced.

_modifiedClasses.label: Stovepipe
_modifiedClasses.note: The connector between appliance and chimney. WETT treats appliance, connector and chimney as one system with three parts, and this is the part with no other home. Corrected 2026-08-05 — the connector is swept with the chimney. Declaring zero implied it was not.

_modifiedClasses.label: Propane tank
_modifiedClasses.note: Usually leased, and the lease is a fact worth carrying — `owned-or-rented` does the same job here it does for a rented water heater. Zero care is a ruling, and it is a contractual fact as much as a technical one: the tank is usually leased and the supplier maintains it.

_modifiedClasses.label: Oil tank
_modifiedClasses.note: Insurance-relevant rather than merely condition-relevant. Age and type drive coverage, which is why the opportunity fires on age rather than on a finding. Zero care is a ruling — the shell and fittings are inspected, and everything else is a licensed trade's.

_modifiedClasses.label: Propane regulator
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling: a regulator is inspected and replaced on a horizon. HouseSteady labour cannot touch gas at all.

_modifiedClasses.label: Oil tank fill and vent
_modifiedClasses.note: TSSA-regulated and separate from the shell — a sound tank with a wrong fill or vent is a real and separate finding. Zero care is a ruling — TSSA-regulated and inspected only.

_modifiedClasses.label: Electrical panel
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care categories, and that is the ruling rather than an omission: every act that would maintain a panel is licensed electrical work. Three of its four inspection points are the whole of what can be honestly said from outside the enclosure, and the fourth is access-gated on an electrician already being there. Zero care is a ruling.

_modifiedClasses.label: Whole-home surge protector
_modifiedClasses.note: Sacrificial by design and it reports its own death on a small light nobody looks at. One inspection point, high value, and it is exactly the kind of thing a documented house catches and an undocumented one does not. Zero care is a ruling and it follows from the design: it is sacrificial. Nothing maintains it; the status light reports its death.

_modifiedClasses.label: Service mast and meter base
_modifiedClasses.note: Exposed to trees, ice and storms on rural lots while the interior panel is untouched. Regional. Zero care is a ruling — inspected from the ground, and every remedy is a licensed electrician's.

_modifiedClasses.label: GFCI outlet
_modifiedClasses.note: Its one care-adjacent act — pressing test and reset — is inspection under the owner's line: operating a device to learn is not altering a circuit. Zero care is a ruling.

_modifiedClasses.label: Transfer switch
_modifiedClasses.note: Zero care is a ruling: it is exercised as part of the generator's run rather than on its own rhythm.

_modifiedClasses.label: Generator inlet and interlock
_modifiedClasses.note: A portable generator often connects through one of these rather than a transfer switch, and a cord back-feeding a dryer outlet with no interlock is the failure this class exists to name. Zero care is a ruling — an inlet and an interlock are inspected, not maintained.

_modifiedClasses.label: Solar inverter
_modifiedClasses.note: Shortest lifespan in a solar system by a wide margin, which is the entire reason it is not merged with the array. Zero care is a ruling: sealed, and its ventilation clearance is an inspection point rather than a task.

_howToApply: Append the five arrays. Then REPLACE each entry in `_modifiedClasses` by id — 45 classes, all changes confined to `careCategories` and `note`.
